Intestinal malrotation: The patient's symptoms, laboratory results, and imaging findings are consistent with intestinal malrotation. The abnormal position of the transverse colon and small-bowel loops, abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, and mesenteric congestion support this diagnosis.
Midgut volvulus: The patient's symptoms, such as acute hypogastric pain and nausea, and the imaging findings suggesting mesenteric congestion and an abnormal position of the small-bowel loops, are also consistent with midgut volvulus.
